title: Direction Audit v1
description: An agent's audit of whether each protocol metric's declared direction (higher/lower is better) matches the metric's own definition. It exists because direction is decided by a model during `protocol propose` and then consumed everywhere as fact: on a real FDG protocol every metric, including 'principal-angle mismatch of per-client separating bases' and a separating-vs-nuisance prototype variance, was declared direction=higher, so a near-orthogonal 79-degree mismatch and a huge variance were both read as improvements. No deterministic check can catch that from the artifact alone — spotting it means reading the definition, which is a judgement, so it is asked of an agent. The platform keeps the consequence: a metric this audit calls inconsistent is never allowed to carry a scientific verdict.

consistent.description: True when the declared direction matches what the definition says the number measures.

reasoning.description: Which part of the definition decides it, in the terms the definition uses.

evidence.description: Quoted text from the metric definition. A direction claim with no quote is a guess about the measurement.

inconsistent.description: Metric names whose declared direction contradicts their definition. Recomputed by the platform from the findings, because a model that forgets to list one must not be able to make the inconsistency disappear.
